_about.what: The rules for the self-explaining parts check. It says which files count as parts, what their header must hold, and the grade limit.
_about.why: Rules kept in data can change with one edit. The script holds no lists of its own, so nothing is hard coded.
_about.how: Edit a value, then run node scripts/check-self-explaining.mjs. Each list has a reason next to it. Add a reason when you add an entry.
_about.next: Read the concept page named in concept_page to see why each part explains itself.

sections_why: The four lines of a self-explaining part. The first label of each is the one to write. The second labels (What it is, Why it matters) are the ones the concept pages already use for the same idea, so those pages count without a rewrite.

where.script: to the comment block at the top of the file
where.markdown: to the front matter as what:, why:, how:, next:, or as labelled lines near the top of the page
where.json: to an "_about" object at the top of the file, under the keys what, why, how and next
where.schema: to the schema's top "description", as labelled sentences

head_lines_why: A header belongs at the top. 60 lines leaves room for a long top comment and front matter.
max_grade_why: The owner's bar: every surface a person reads is at Flesch-Kincaid grade 8.0 or below. Tuned on the concept pages, the known-good headers: run node scripts/check-self-explaining.mjs and each of them passes at this limit.

grade_ignore_patterns.`[^`]*`: code in backticks is a name to type, not prose to read
grade_ignore_patterns.https?://\\S+: a link is not read as words
grade_ignore_patterns.\\S*/\\S*: a file path is a name, not prose
grade_ignore_patterns.\\S+\\.(?:mjs|cjs|js|json|md|sh|py|ts)\\: a file name is a name, not prose
grade_ignore_patterns.--[a-z][a-z-]*: a command flag is a name to type
grade_ignore_patterns.\\{\\{[^}]*\\}\\}: a name token is replaced before anyone reads it

name_words.why: A word of the file name must show up in the What or Why line (or a doc's title). Words that only say what kind of file it is (check, test, schema, config) say nothing about what it does, so they do not count. match_prefix: the first five letters are enough, so 'explaining' matches 'explains'.

known_misleading_why: Names that mislead in a way the word match cannot catch. Each entry: path, why it misleads, and fixed_by (how it was fixed). An entry with no fixed_by fails the check. None are known in this repository.
changed_parts_must_pass_why: A part in the baseline that someone edits must get its header in the same change. That is how the baseline shrinks.

scope.include_why: Every script, test, schema, data file and doc a person meets when they open the repo.

formats_why: Each kind of file keeps its header in its own place. A .sql schema is read like a script, from its -- comments. A file with no extension counts as a script when its first line starts with #!.

exempt.docs/LESSONS.md: generated by scripts/lessons-feed.mjs; its generator owns the header
exempt.docs/SHOWCASE.md: generated by scripts/showcase.mjs; its generator owns the header
exempt.CHANGELOG.md: generated by git-cliff from commit messages
exempt.AGENTS.md: being rewritten by its own change (the agent rules rewrite); it comes into scope when that lands

baseline_about.what: The parts that had no full header when the self-explaining check began, each with a fingerprint of its text.
baseline_about.why: The check must not fail on old files all at once. This list lets them wait, and it only shrinks.
baseline_about.how: Do not add to it. When you fix a part, run node scripts/check-self-explaining.mjs --update-baseline to drop it. A part you edit leaves the list and must pass.
baseline_about.next: Pick a part from this list, give it its four lines, and run the update.

parts_map.banner: generated by scripts/parts-map.mjs from each part's header; do not edit by hand
parts_map.count_line: {parts} parts. {passing} explain themselves. The rest are in the baseline and get their header when next changed.

front_matter.title: Parts map
front_matter.what: A list of every part of this repo, each with one line on what it is.
front_matter.why: Open one page and see all the parts. You do not need to open each file to learn what it does.
front_matter.how: Find a part by its folder. Click it to open it. The line next to it is the part's own What this is line.
front_matter.next: Run node scripts/parts-map.mjs after you add a part. The check fails if this page is out of date.
